description: Given Prefect Slack notifications — SlackWebhook block, @flow/@task on_failure/on_completion hooks, Prefect Automation Slack actions, or a plain @task calling slack_sdk directly — determine whether the message is a run-status notification (pipeline- or task-scoped Orchestra alerts: block, destination not connection_id) or an explicit mid-flow pipeline step (SLACK integration task with SEND_SLACK_MESSAGE), and author the corresponding YAML.

evals.prompt: Convert this Prefect Slack failure hook to an Orchestra pipeline-level alert (see files/slack_flow_failure_hook.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live sends, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A pipeline-level alerts: entry firing on FAILED with a single SLACK destination (destination: '#eng-oncall', no connection_id field) — the literal channel carried straight through.

assertions.text: The SLACK destination sets destination (SLACK/EMAIL require destination, not connection_id)
The #eng-oncall channel is carried over as the SLACK destination value
connection_id is NOT set on the SLACK destination — Slack alerts resolve from the workspace Slack connection; connection_id is only required for PAGER_DUTY/TEAMS/WEBHOOK/DATADOG

evals.prompt: Convert this Prefect task-level Slack success hook to an Orchestra task-level alert on the load_warehouse task only — it should not fire for the whole flow (see files/slack_task_success_hook.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live sends, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A task-level alerts: entry on the load-warehouse task (not the pipeline root) firing on SUCCEEDED with a SLACK destination (destination: '#warehouse-notifications', no connection_id field), since a task-scoped hook maps to a task-level alert, not a flow-wide hook.

assertions.text: The SLACK destination sets destination (SLACK/EMAIL require destination, not connection_id)
The #warehouse-notifications channel is carried over as the SLACK destination value
The alert is placed on the load-warehouse TaskModel (task-level), not the pipeline root alerts: block — matching the task-scoped @task(on_completion=...) hook rather than a flow-wide hook
extract_data, which has no hook, does not also get this alert

evals.prompt: This Prefect flow posts a Slack message mid-run, after the dbt build finishes and before the downstream load starts (see files/slack_mid_flow_raw_client.py). Convert this to the appropriate Orchestra pipeline construct — this is a workflow step, not a status notification, even though it never imports prefect_slack. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live sends, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A SLACK pipeline task (integration: SLACK, integration_job: SEND_SLACK_MESSAGE) with parameters.channel_name '#data-team' and text set, wired via depends_on so it runs after the run_dbt_build task and before load_downstream — NOT an alerts: block, since this is an explicit step whose position in the run matters, and the raw slack_sdk.WebClient call is still a Slack notification despite not importing prefect_slack.

assertions.text: Output is a valid YAML document
A SLACK integration task is present
The task sets a channel_name parameter
The #data-team channel is carried over as the channel_name value

This is expressed as a SLACK/SEND_SLACK_MESSAGE task wired via depends_on, not an alerts: block, since the message is a positioned mid-run step rather than a run-status notification — despite the source task never importing prefect_slack
The task's depends_on reflects it firing after the dbt build task and before the downstream load task, preserving the source's execution order
